core_obligations: Global generation and Cohen-Macaulayness (proof lines 2584-2596): the twist on the blowup is very ample by construction, so its restriction to the exceptional divisisor is very ample; the blowup is normal, so the exceptional divisor, being an effective Cartier divisor on a normal scheme, is Cohen-Macaulay.

Cohomology and sections of the twists (proof lines 2596-2608): the computation of the sections and the vanishing for the powers of the ideal sheaf, applied to the short exact sequences comparing consecutive powers and the associated long exact cohomology sequences, gives the vanishing of the first cohomology and the identification of the sections of the twists with the successive quotients of the powers of the maximal ideal.

Degree computation (proof lines 2608-2615): the degree of the twist is the difference of Euler characteristics, which by the previous identifications equals the embedding dimension of the maximal ideal minus one; since for a local ring of dimension two this embedding dimension is at least two with equality exactly for regular local rings, the degree is at least one with equality only in the regular case.
proof_roadmap: Get very ampleness of the twist and Cohen-Macaulayness of the exceptional curve.
Use the comparison sequences of powers of the ideal sheaf for the cohomology and the sections.
Compute the degree through the Euler characteristic and read off the regularity criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the exceptional divisor of the blowup in the rational situation is a proper Cohen-Macaulay curve with very ample twist of degree at least one, with equality only when the base is regular, with vanishing first cohomology and with sections of the twists identified with the successive quotients of the powers of the maximal ideal (statement lines 2580-2594). The proof (proof lines 2595-2615) uses very ampleness, normality, the comparison sequences of powers of the ideal sheaf, and a degree computation. H3: five assertions proved together from several inputs.
